questions.q: If 5 workers take 10 days to finish a wall, what is the product of the number of workers and the number of days?
questions.a: The product is 50. A student answering "15" or "2" is likely confusing inverse proportion with addition or direct division, failing to recognize that the relationship relies on multiplication.

questions.q: Why does the time taken to complete a task decrease when more workers are added?
questions.a: Because the total amount of work is fixed; adding more hands to the job means each person does a smaller share of the work, finishing the project faster. An answer stating "it just happens" shows a lack of conceptual understanding of the "fixed total" requirement.

questions.q: A car travels at 40 km/h and reaches a destination in 6 hours. If the speed is increased to 80 km/h, how long will the journey take?
questions.a: Step 1: Product = 40 × 6 = 240. Step 2: New speed = 80. Step 3: Time = 240 / 80 = 3 hours. A student who guesses "12 hours" is incorrectly applying direct proportion (thinking more speed means more time).

questions.q: If a machine produces 100 items in 2 hours, and a faster machine produces 200 items in the same 2 hours, is this an inverse proportion? Why?
questions.a: No, this is not inverse proportion. In inverse proportion, one variable must decrease as the other increases, whereas here, the number of items increased while the time stayed the same.

questions.q: Two friends are packing books. If they take 4 hours, would 4 friends take 2 hours or 8 hours? Justify your choice.
questions.a: They would take 2 hours. Since the number of workers doubled (from 2 to 4), the time must be halved (from 4 to 2) to keep the total work product constant at 8.

questions.q: Create a real-world scenario involving inverse proportion that is NOT about workers or time.
questions.a: Example: "A fixed amount of money (₹100) is used to buy pens. If the price per pen increases, the number of pens you can buy decreases." A poor answer would be "Buying more apples costs more money," which is direct, not inverse, proportion.
